chunks: "I work backwards from the allowed output droop and ripple. The flying capacitor sets the slow-switching output resistance, R SSL equals 1 over (fC fly) .
For a doubler at 500 kilohertz and 1 microfarads that's 2 ohms, against about 8 ohms from four switch resistances, so making C fly bigger past a point buys almost nothing.
A good rule is to choose it so R SSL is no more than the switch-limited resistance: here 0. 25 microfarads is the floor and 1 microfarads is comfortable.
It supplies the load alone for half a cycle, so change in V equals I over (2fC out) ; for 20 milliamps, 500 kilohertz and 10 microfarads that's 2 millivolts, plus ESR times the current step.
Then the part I'd actually check is what the capacitor really is in the circuit. Ceramics lose capacitance with DC bias: a 1 microfarads 0402 X5R at 3.
3 volts may hold only half of that. So I'd specify the effective value at the working voltage and temperature, with a rating at least 1.
5 to 2 times the voltage across it, X7R or X5R in a decent case size, low ESR, and enough RMS current rating: 2I out in the flying cap.
And put them right at the pins to keep loop inductance down."
